original_question: Let K be a compact connected subset of R^n, and let p and q be points of K. For every epsilon > 0, does there exist a curve gamma connecting p to q such that the total length of the part of gamma lying outside K is less than epsilon?
target_in_paper: Section 6, "Shortcut in a connected set" — the open problem asking whether two points in a compact connected subset of Euclidean space can be joined by a curve that spends arbitrarily small length outside the set.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual question. It correctly has: a compact connected set K, points p,q in K, Euclidean ambient space R^n, the quantifier "for every epsilon > 0," and the key requirement that the curve may leave K but should do so with arbitrarily small total outside-length.
missing_details: The paper's wording should be read as a question about a curve in the ambient Euclidean space R^n joining p to q, not necessarily a curve contained in K.
To make the question fully stand-alone, it helps to specify that the curve is a continuous map gamma:[0,1]->R^n with gamma(0)=p and gamma(1)=q.
What is controlled is only the Euclidean length of the portion of gamma lying in R^n\K; the paper does not ask for gamma itself to have small total length or to remain rectifiable inside K.
No extra hypotheses on K are assumed beyond compactness and connectedness: in particular, K need not be locally connected or path connected.
The nearby context emphasizes that this matters because compact connected sets can contain no nontrivial paths at all (for example, the pseudoarc).

The paper also records that the case n=2 is already known by Banakh, so the intended unresolved scope is the general Euclidean-dimension version, even though the stated problem itself is phrased for K subset of R^n without excluding n=2.
refined_question: Let K be a compact connected subset of R^n, and let p,q in K. Is it true that for every epsilon>0 there exists a continuous curve gamma:[0,1]->R^n with gamma(0)=p and gamma(1)=q such that the portion of gamma lying in R^n\K has total Euclidean length less than epsilon?
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper: Section 6 states exactly this open problem under the title "Shortcut in a connected set." Your epsilon-version is a faithful unpacking of the paper's phrase "the length of gamma\K is arbitrarily small." The only real sharpening needed is to make explicit that gamma is a curve in the ambient Euclidean space joining p to q and that only the length spent outside K is constrained. The surrounding context in the same section adds two paper-faithful clarifications: first, K need not contain any nontrivial path (pseudoarc example), and second, the planar case n=2 is already known by Banakh, so the open content is really the higher-dimensional/general Euclidean case.
